Conseillers immobiliers : organisez vos: Estate agents: organise seller updates, viewing feedback and reports when there are no viewings, with a simple structure and dated next steps.
Convenez d’un rythme de nouvelles avec c: Agree an update schedule with each seller, keep the facts in one record and end every report with a dated next step. Even without viewings, explain what you have done, what you have observed and what you suggest testing. This is an organisational method to adapt to your portfolio and the commitments in your agency agreements, not a guarantee of a sale.
1. Fixer un rendez-vous de suivi, pas se: 1. Schedule an update, rather than just intending to send one
Au lancement, choisissez ensemble le can: At the start of marketing, agree the preferred channel, the date of the next update and the topics to review. A weekly report can be a starting point if you can sustain that frequency. Block out time in your diary and record the next deadline in each property file. Feedback after a viewing complements this appointment; it does not replace it.
2. Garder une fiche courte et exploitabl: 2. Keep a short, actionable record for each property
Votre fiche doit permettre de préparer u: Your record should let you prepare a conversation without rereading every message. Keep these five fields in your usual tool:
Période et actions : dates du bilan, dif: Period and actions: reporting dates, checked listings, updated presentation and work actually carried out.
Résultats observés : demandes, visites e: Observed results: enquiries, viewings and offers, with their source. Unavailable data stays ‘unavailable’, not zero.
Retours : points appréciés, freins expri: Feedback: positive points, stated concerns and unanswered questions, without turning an impression into an intention to buy.
Analyse : hypothèses à vérifier, distinc: Analysis: hypotheses to check, separate from facts. Few enquiries alone do not show that price is the only problem.
Suite : action proposée, personne chargé: Next step: proposed action, person responsible and review date.
3. Après une visite, restituer les faits: 3. After a viewing, report the facts before drawing conclusions
Demandez ce qui convient, ce qui bloque: Ask what works, what is holding the person back and what they see as the next step. Note their answers, then prepare an accurate update for the seller. If the buyer has not replied yet, say so and schedule a follow-up. Avoid ‘very positive viewing’ without specifics: liking a room is not an offer.
Le compte rendu comme outil de communica: Reporting as a communication tool is also covered by
Vérifiez d’abord que l’annonce est bien: First check that the listing is visible, that photos and information match the property and that enquiries have been handled. Then compare available feedback with the previous period on a like-for-like basis. Do not add views from different portals as though they were unique people. Suggest a specific adjustment and set a date to review its effects.

Sur la période examinée, aucune visite n: There were no viewings during the period reviewed. The listings have been checked. Statistics from one portal are unavailable, so I cannot draw a conclusion about visibility there. I suggest clarifying the description of access to the property and reviewing progress on the agreed date. This scenario illustrates a method; it is not a case handled by Guillaume.
5. Utiliser le point d’équipe pour déblo: 5. Use team discussions to move an action forward
Apportez un dossier anonymisé et une que: Bring an anonymised case and a specific question: how should this concern be phrased, what information is missing or what could be tested? Leave with an action, not just a general opinion. Assess your organisation by reports sent on the agreed date and files with no next step. These indicators track your work; they predict neither sales nor income.

Can you become a real estate advisor without a degree?
Oui, en France, une personne physique pe: Yes. In France, an individual can work as an independent real estate advisor under commercial agent status without a specific real estate degree. They must, however, act on behalf of a professional who holds the real estate professional card, under a mandate, with RSAC registration and a CCI collaborator certificate requested by the cardholder. This route does not allow them to present themselves as an estate agent holding their own card.

Legally, the real estate commercial agent—also called an independent real estate negotiator—negotiates in the name of and on behalf of the principal. The professional cardholder oversees the mandate and requests the certificate authorising the individual collaborator to negotiate.
